job.title: Payroll Officer
job.description:
Payroll Officer | Gladesville | $110K + Super
 
THE COMPANY
Join an established Australian owned organisation with a long history and a significant presence across manufacturing and industrial operations.
With a large, diverse workforce and operations running around the clock, payroll is a critical function within the business. You’ll be joining an experienced and supportive payroll team at an exciting time, with the organisation currently preparing for a major payroll systems transformation.
This is a stable business that values reliability, quality and getting things right, and they are looking for an experienced Payroll Officer who takes the same approach to their work.
 
THE ROLE
Working as part of an established payroll team, you’ll take ownership of a weekly payroll of approximately 450 predominantly manufacturing employees within a complex, fast-paced environment.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing end-to-end weekly payroll from timesheet through to finalisation
  • Extracting and reviewing employee hours from Kronos and processing through MicroPay
  • Maintaining employee master data and processing payroll changes
  • Processing allowances, deductions, leave, manual pays, back pays and salary increases
  • Reviewing audit reports and investigating payroll discrepancies
  • Managing workers compensation payments and reconciliations
  • Completing payroll, superannuation, PAYG and deduction reconciliations and uploads
  • Preparing payroll tax across NSW, VIC and WA
  • Processing GL information and providing payroll reporting to Finance
  • Responding to employee payroll queries and liaising with external bodies including the ATO and Centrelink
  • Supporting the broader payroll team during peak periods
  • Contributing to the payroll function as the business transitions from MicroPay to SAP
The role sits within a team of three Payroll Officers and a Payroll Time & Attendance Officer, so while you’ll have ownership of your payroll, you’ll also have support around you.
 
THE CANDIDATE
We’re looking for an experienced Payroll Officer who is comfortable taking genuine ownership of an end-to-end payroll and understands the deadlines and complexities that come with a large weekly workforce.
You’ll ideally bring:
  • Strong end-to-end payroll experience within a medium to large organisation
  • Experience managing weekly payrolls, ideally within manufacturing, industrial or another award/EBA-driven environment
  • MicroPay experience will be highly regarded
  • Experience with Kronos or another time & attendance system
  • Sound knowledge of payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG, leave and payroll reconciliations
  • Confidence working with high volumes and tight weekly deadlines
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies
  • A collaborative, team-focused approach
  • The confidence to work autonomously and take responsibility for your payroll
Experience with SAP would be advantageous given the upcoming system transition, but it isn’t essential.
 
THE BENEFITS
This one will particularly suit someone who values stability, flexibility around their working day and being part of a close-knit payroll team.
  • Circa $110K + Super, with some flexibility depending on experience
  • Permanent, stable opportunity with an established Australian business
  • Flexible start and finish times : 8:00am–4:00pm, 8:30am–4:30pm or similar
  • Supportive and experienced payroll team
  • Ownership of a substantial weekly payroll
  • Exposure to a major MicroPay to SAP transformation
  • Time off in lieu available where additional hours are required
  • Opportunity to work within a complex 24/7 manufacturing environment
  • Five days onsite, ideal for someone who enjoys being part of the team and close to the operation

job.title: Procurement Officer
job.description:
Procurement Officer 
Commercial Procurement, Supplier Management, Sourcing & Negotiation  

If you're a procurement professional who enjoys getting behind the numbers, challenging suppliers, negotiating better commercial outcomes and finding smarter ways to secure supply, this could be a very interesting next move.
We're working with a well-established, global organisation within th e packaging and manufacturing sector to appoint a commercially minded Procurement Officer.
This is a hands-on procurement role with genuine commercial responsibility and exposure to a broad supplier network.
What you'll actually be doingYou'll work directly with suppliers to:
  • Negotiate pricing, contracts, lead times, MOQs and commercial terms
  • Manage and develop key supplier relationships
  • Source new and alternative suppliers
  • Run supplier quotes, tenders and commercial reviews
  • Challenge and negotiate supplier price increases
  • Monitor supplier performance across cost, quality, service and delivery
  • Identify and mitigate supply risks before they become problems
  • Work closely with Supply Planning, Purchasing, Sales, Customer Service, Quality, Operations and Finance
  • Analyse supplier pricing, spend, performance and market movements
  • Support new business opportunities through competitive sourcing
  • Drive supplier improvement and corrective actions
  • Contribute to procurement projects, process improvement and ERP/data initiatives
In other words, you'll have genuine influence over what the business buys, who it buys it from and what it pays.

We're interested in procurement professionals who have already had exposure to commercial supplier management and negotiation.
You might currently be a:

We're looking for approximately 3–5 years' relevant experience, ideally gained within:
  • Procurement / purchasing
  • Manufacturing
  • Packaging
  • FMCG / consumer goods
  • Distribution / wholesale
  • Supply chain
  • Logistics
  • Another commercially focused supplier environment
You don't necessarily need packaging experience.
What's more important is that you can demonstrate:
✔ You've negotiated with suppliers — not just ordered from them
✔ You're comfortable challenging pricing and commercial terms
✔ You can build strong supplier relationships while still holding suppliers accountable
✔ You understand lead times, supply risk, quality and service
✔ You're commercially and analytically minded
✔ You're confident working with ERP systems and Excel
✔ You can manage multiple suppliers, projects and priorities

Why this role?
This is an opportunity to move beyond transactional purchasing and develop your career across commercial procurement, sourcing, negotiation and supplier management.
You'll gain exposure to a broad supplier base and be involved in procurement decisions that directly impact cost, margin, supply continuity and customer outcomes.
And importantly, you don't need to have managed a team to be successful here.
We're looking for someone who is commercially sharp, curious, confident with suppliers and ready to take ownership.

If that's how you naturally approach procurement, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Operational Safety Manager
job.description:
Operational Safety Manager   |  Western Sydney  |  $150K to $170K + Super

The Company:

Step into a fast-growing, privately-owned operator in a highly regulated, safety-critical industry, with an evolving and expanding service offering. Safety isn't a compliance box here. It's a genuine leadership priority, backed by real authority and real investment, and our client is looking for someone who wants to help shape what safety looks like, not just maintain what already exists.

This is a newly defined Operational Safety Manager role, created because the business is ready to invest properly in safety leadership, not just fill a gap. It comes with a clear runway to a broader Head of Safety and Compliance position for the right person, giving you a real say in how the function grows from here.

The Position:

Reporting directly to the General Manager, you'll take genuine ownership of operational safety, not oversight from a distance, leading a ground-up review of current procedures with the mandate to reshape how safety works from day one.

What you'll be doing:
  • Leading a full, ground-up review of current safety procedures and driving practical improvements
  • Rebuilding and maintaining SWMS, risk assessments and safe operating procedures
  • Owning incident and near-miss investigations end to end, from first response and root cause analysis through to corrective actions and close-out
  • Building operational readiness for dangerous goods handling and storage, including training, risk assessments and emergency response procedures
  • Leading safety training, coaching and toolbox talks across drivers, plant operators and site teams
  • Driving a genuine, measurable shift in safety culture, particularly building trust and buy-in within driver and operational teams
  • Overseeing Chain of Responsibility and heavy vehicle safety at the operational level, including fatigue, loading and scheduling risk
  • Managing Return to Work and Workers Compensation cases from notification through to resolution
  • Coordinating emergency preparedness, including planning, drills, and post-incident review
  • Exercising full stop-work authority where you identify unsafe activity, backed by senior leadership
  • Partnering closely with senior operational leaders across the business to embed safety into day-to-day decision-making
  • Reporting on safety performance and trends to the General Manager, with a clear line of sight to broader compliance and business risk
The Candidate:

We're looking for someone genuinely progressive in how they think about safety, someone who sees it as a driver of performance and culture, not just a regulatory requirement. This role suits an experienced, dynamic safety leader who wants to build and shape something, not simply administer an existing system.

You'll bring:
  • Significant experience in a senior operational safety or WHS leadership role within transport, waste, logistics, industrial or another high-risk, regulated environment
  • Solid working knowledge of Chain of Responsibility, NHVR requirements, and heavy vehicle or bulk transport safety
  • A strong track record of leading incident investigations and translating findings into real, followed procedures
  • Genuine comfort operating in yards, depots and vehicles, not a desk-bound safety professional
  • The confidence to challenge unsafe practices and influence change at every level of a business, regardless of commercial pressure
  • Experience with, or strong exposure to, dangerous goods, chemical handling or petrochemical environments (highly regarded, not essential)
  • Background with a larger, structured logistics or industrial organisation is a plus, but we're just as open to a hands-on operator from a smaller business who's ready to step up
The Benefits:
  • $150,000 to $170,000 + super
  • A newly created role with genuine scope to shape safety strategy and execution from day one
  • A clear, realistic progression pathway to a Head of Safety and Compliance role
  • Full authority and senior leadership backing to make safety decisions that matter
  • Involvement in a major growth initiative: the safe expansion into dangerous goods
  • A hands-on, high-impact culture where your work is visible and valued, not lost in bureaucracy
  • The chance to build modern, practical safety systems in a business that's genuinely investing in getting it right

job.title: CREDIT OFFICER
job.description:
Credit Officer | Eastern Creek | $80K + Super | Immediate Start

Take Ownership. Build Relationships. Make an Impact.
Are you a Credit Officer who enjoys more than just chasing debt?
Do you thrive on building relationships, solving problems and taking ownership of your ledger from start to finish?
If you're looking for a permanent opportunity where your experience will be valued, your ideas welcomed and your contribution recognised, this could be the role for you.

The Company
Our client is a well-established Australian success story with a reputation built on quality products, exceptional customer service and long-standing customer relationships.
With continued growth and a supportive, down-to-earth culture, they are looking for an experienced Credit Officer to join their finance team and play a key role in maintaining strong customer relationships and healthy cash flow.
This is the kind of business where people stay because they're trusted, supported and genuinely enjoy coming to work.

The Opportunity
This is a true end-to-end credit position offering plenty of variety and autonomy.
You'll take ownership of your ledger, managing everything from credit applications and account setup through to collections, reconciliations, dispute resolution and customer relationship management.
Working closely with customers, sales teams and finance colleagues, you'll become a trusted point of contact who can balance commercial outcomes with exceptional customer service.
No two days will be the same, making this an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys being busy, building relationships and making things happen.

Key Responsibilities
  • Assess and approve new credit applications
  • Conduct credit checks and customer reference verification
  • Set up and maintain customer accounts
  • Manage collections and follow up outstanding accounts
  • Resolve customer disputes and account queries
  • Perform account reconciliations and investigate discrepancies
  • Process credit notes, refunds and manual invoices
  • Monitor ageing reports and proactively reduce overdue debt
  • Build strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders
  • Support month-end reporting and credit administration activities
  • Work closely with sales and operations teams to achieve positive outcomes

About You
You'll bring:
  • Previous experience in a Credit Officer position
  • Strong end-to-end credit management experience
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
  • A confident but professional approach to collections
  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills
  • The ability to prioritise and manage a busy workload
  • Intermediate Excel skills
  • A proactive attitude and genuine desire to provide great customer service
  • Experience working in a fast-paced environment

What's On Offer?
  • $80,000 + Super
  • Permanent full-time opportunity
  • Immediate start available
  • Stable business with a strong market reputation
  • Friendly and supportive team culture
  • On-site parking
  • Varied role with plenty of autonomy
  • Opportunity to make your mark and genuinely add value
  • Long-term career opportunity with a stable Australian organisation

job.title: Assistant Payroll Manager
job.description:
Assistant Payroll Manager | North Parramatta | Permanent | Lead an established payroll team | Onsite parking | Hybrid – 1 day WFH after probation
 
The Company
Join a well-established Australian business with a significant national footprint and a strong reputation in its industry. With continued growth across the group, the payroll function is expanding and this newly created Assistant Payroll Manager position will provide additional leadership across a large and experienced team.
Based in North Parramatta, you'll join a collaborative environment where Payroll works closely with Finance, HR and the broader business.
The Role
Reporting to the Head of Payroll & HR Services, you'll take a hands-on leadership role across the day-to-day payroll function, overseeing payroll operations across multiple entities while leading and developing a team of payroll professionals.
This isn't just about making sure payroll gets out the door. You'll be a key point of support for the team and senior stakeholders, while also looking at how processes, systems and ways of working can continue to improve.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading the day-to-day payroll function, ensuring accurate and timely processing across multiple entities
  • Mentoring, coaching and developing the payroll team while driving consistency and high service standards
  • Overseeing payroll compliance including awards, minimum wage reviews, superannuation and internal procedures
  • Managing payroll schedules, annual salary reviews, profit share payments and month-end reporting
  • Partnering with senior leaders around onboarding, payroll matters and issue resolution
  • Overseeing employee payroll administration including salary changes, terminations and employee enquiries
  • Maintaining payroll procedures and documentation to ensure strong governance and compliance
  • Identifying opportunities to improve payroll processes, systems and operational efficiencies
  • Working closely with HR, Finance and IT to deliver improvements across the payroll function
About You
We're looking for an experienced payroll professional who knows their stuff technically but, just as importantly, genuinely enjoys leading and developing people.
You'll ideally bring:
  • Previous experience leading or supervising a payroll team
  • Strong end-to-end payroll knowledge within a complex, high-volume or multi-entity environment
  • Sound knowledge of Australian payroll legislation, awards, superannuation and compliance requirements
  • Strong Excel skills and confidence working with payroll data and reporting
  • A collaborative and supportive leadership style with the ability to coach and develop others
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
  • The ability to investigate issues, solve problems and confidently make decisions
  • A continuous improvement mindset and an interest in making payroll processes better, not simply maintaining the status quo
  • Experience with Micropay and/or ConnX would be highly regarded
What's On Offer?
This is a great opportunity for an experienced Payroll Team Leader, Payroll Supervisor or 2IC who is ready to step into a broader leadership role, or an established Assistant Payroll Manager looking for a role where they can have genuine impact.
  • Permanent full-time opportunity
  • North Parramatta location with onsite parking
  • Hybrid working with 1 day WFH after probation
  • Newly created position with genuine scope to influence the payroll function
  • Established and experienced payroll team
  • Opportunity to drive process improvement and system enhancements
  • Long-term career opportunities within a large national organisation
If you're an experienced payroll leader who enjoys developing people, improving processes and being close to the day-to-day operation, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Procurement Manager - Wetherill Park
job.description:
Procurement Manager  Brisbane or Sydney

Are you the procurement person who walks into a business and thinks, “We can do this better”?

This is not a role for someone who simply manages POs, renews supplier contracts and keeps the wheels turning.
We’re looking for a commercially sharp Procurement Manager, killer negotiator and dynamic leader who can take ownership of procurement, challenge the status quo and help shape what great looks like.With a new executive team and a clear focus on growth, this is your opportunity to step in, assess what’s working, challenge what isn’t and build a smarter, more commercially effective procurement function.The opportunityYou’ll lead procurement across ANZ, taking ownership of sourcing, supplier performance, negotiations, purchasing governance and commercial outcomes.You’ll work closely with the new executive leadership team and key stakeholders across Supply Chain, Sales, Operations, Finance, Quality and Customer Service — bringing commercial thinking, energy and fresh ideas to the table.
Your mandate?Improve it. Challenge it. Negotiate harder. Find better ways of doing it.
You’ll have genuine scope to influence processes, supplier strategy, systems and ways of working rather than simply inheriting a procurement playbook and following it.

What you’ll be doing
  • Own and execute procurement and sourcing strategies across key spend categories
  • Lead high-value supplier negotiations across pricing, terms, service and contracts
  • Identify new and alternative suppliers to improve competitiveness and reduce supply risk
  • Drive supplier performance, accountability, service levels and commercial outcomes
  • Lead tenders, commercial reviews, renewals and sourcing initiatives
  • Identify and deliver cost savings, margin improvement and supply efficiencies
  • Challenge existing processes and introduce smarter, more disciplined ways of working
  • Improve procurement governance, purchasing controls, data and reporting
  • Work with the executive team to identify opportunities and turn them into action
  • Use procurement data, market intelligence and supplier insights to make better commercial decisions
  • Lead and develop a small Procurement team, providing coaching, direction and accountability
  • Support D365 optimisation and broader systems/process improvement
  • Partner across the business to solve supply, pricing, inventory and supplier issues quickly
Who are we looking for? We’re looking for someone with energy, commercial nous and the confidence to make things happen.
You’ll ideally bring:
  • 5+ years’ procurement, strategic sourcing or senior purchasing experience
  • Experience operating at Procurement Manager or senior procurement level
  • Outstanding negotiation skills — you know how to get the best commercial outcome without destroying the supplier relationship
  • Strong experience across supplier management, sourcing, tenders and commercial reviews
  • Ideally, a background in commercial plastic packaging, packaging, manufacturing, distribution, FMCG or a similar environment
  • Demonstrated success delivering cost savings, efficiencies or improved supplier performance
  • Experience leading, coaching or developing a small team
  • Strong commercial and analytical capability
  • ERP experience — D365 is highly regarded
  • The confidence to challenge senior stakeholders and suppliers when necessary
  • A genuine continuous-improvement mindset
Most importantly, what’s your attitude?We want someone who gets things done.

Someone who doesn’t accept “that’s how we’ve always done it” as an answer.
You’ll be comfortable getting into the detail, asking difficult questions, negotiating hard, bringing people with you and then actually implementing the change.

You’ll need to be dynamic, commercially hungry, pragmatic and solutions-focused.
You’ll also need the maturity to know when to push, when to listen and when to bring the team with you.

This is a genuine opportunity to make your mark.

You’ll have the opportunity to reshape procurement practices and the autonomy to identify where the business can do better — commercially, operationally and strategically.

If you’re a Procurement Manager who wants to own the outcome rather than simply manage the process, this could be your next move.
